Summary: BMS Alert list rows have no Edit or Delete action buttons at all
Description: A BMS Alert configuration, once created, can never be edited or deleted through the UI -- its row in the list renders correctly with real data but carries zero action buttons of any kind, unlike every other alert type checked (AC, Ignition, Main Power, Panic, Speed, Idle, Temperature, POI, Vehicle Odometer Alert all have at least one). Found while regression-testing the fix for a previously reported bug (BMS/Odometer Alert list not refreshing), which is otherwise confirmed fixed.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and open Settings > Alert Configuration > BMS Alert.
2. Create a BMS Alert configuration for any vehicle (fill time range, thresholds, notification channel, submit).
3. Confirm the new row appears in the list with correct data.
4. Inspect the row for Edit/Delete action buttons, or try to click one.
5. Repeat steps 1-4 on a different alert type (e.g. Vehicle Odometer Alert or POI Alert) for comparison.
Expected Result: BMS Alert rows should offer the same Edit/Delete action buttons every other alert type's rows do, so a configuration can be managed or removed after creation.
Actual Result: BMS Alert rows have no buttons in the action-column area at all (confirmed live 3x, checking up to 5 rows out of 10 existing rows each time) -- the configuration is permanent once created. Vehicle Odometer Alert and every other alert type checked render their action buttons normally.

Summary: A fixed-position FEEDBACK widget can intercept clicks on real row action buttons underneath it
Description: A "FEEDBACK" button fixed at 40% viewport height on the right edge (position: fixed, not scrolled with page content) is rendered on top of normal page content on at least Dashboard, Unit, and Settings (confirmed absent on Home, Tracking, Reports in the same pass). Because it's fixed to the viewport, any real interactive control (Edit/Delete/Assign/etc.) that happens to scroll to around that screen height -- which depends entirely on how much content renders above it -- becomes genuinely unclickable through a normal click, with no visual indication anything is blocking it. Same class of defect as the already-reported CAN module map-overlay click-interception bug, but this is a shared app-level widget rather than one module's own overlay.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and open a module where the widget renders (e.g. Settings > Vehicle Management > Location Control).
2. Scroll or create enough rows that a row's action button (e.g. Delete) lands at roughly 40% of the viewport height, near the right edge.
3. Attempt a normal click on that action button.
4. Repeat on Dashboard and Unit to confirm the widget also renders there.
Expected Result: The FEEDBACK widget should never sit on top of real, currently-interactive page content -- either it should not intercept pointer events for elements beneath it, or it should be positioned/sized so it can't overlap real controls.
Actual Result: The click does not register on the intended button at all; Playwright's own actionability check reports the FEEDBACK widget's container div as the element intercepting pointer events at that point. Confirmed live 3x: one real click failure during test-data cleanup work, plus two independent module surveys confirming the widget's fixed position and visibility on Dashboard/Unit/Settings.

Summary: [SECURITY] Change Password Stage 1 accepts any password with zero server-side verification
Description: Re-verifying a previously reported bug (Change Password's Verify always rejected the correct password) found the symptom has changed to something more severe: Stage 1's Verify now unlocks Stage 2 for ANY input, including a deliberately wrong password. Network capture during the Verify click shows zero /api/ calls fire at all, for either a correct or incorrect password -- the 'Current password verified' success and Stage 2 unlock are not backed by any server-side check. The Update Password button itself becomes genuinely enabled once a new password is filled in, with Stage 1 'passed' on a wrong password -- the flow is fully prepared to submit a real password change with no current-password verification anywhere in the path. Update Password was deliberately NOT clicked to avoid actually changing the shared staging account's real credentials from a diagnostic script -- whether the final submit endpoint has its own independent check is unknown and needs product-team verification, not further automated probing against the live account.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and open Change Password (Account menu > Change Password).
2. In Stage 1 ("Verify your identity"), enter a definitely-wrong current password (not the real one).
3. Click Verify.
4. Observe whether Stage 2 (New Password / Confirm New Password) unlocks anyway.
5. Fill a new password and confirmation, and check whether Update Password becomes enabled.
6. Do NOT click Update Password on a real/shared account -- stop at confirming the button is enabled.
Expected Result: Verify should call the server to check the current password and only unlock Stage 2 when it is genuinely correct; a wrong password should be rejected with Stage 2 remaining locked.
Actual Result: Stage 2 unlocks and shows a 'Current password verified' success toast for a deliberately wrong password, with zero network calls made during Verify (confirmed via request/response capture). Update Password becomes enabled once a new password is filled in. Confirmed live 3x for the wrong-password-accepted behavior specifically.

Summary: Support ticket list and ticket submission load intermittently slowly
Description: The Support ticket list can take noticeably longer than expected to replace its 'No support tickets found' placeholder with the real ticket data after opening the page -- confirmed live this delay is intermittent (varies between fast and multi-second-slow across repeated checks, not a constant fixed lag). Raising a new ticket via the Raise Ticket dialog can likewise take longer than a typical form submission to return a result. Not a functional failure (both the list and ticket creation do work correctly), but worth investigating as a performance/reliability issue, particularly since a test or user reading the page immediately after load could mistake the placeholder for genuine empty state.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and open Support (Account menu > Support) -- repeat several times across a session.
2. Observe how long the ticket table takes to show real rows vs. the 'No support tickets found' placeholder.
3. Separately, raise a new ticket via Raise Ticket and time how long Submit takes to show a success/error toast.
Expected Result: The ticket list and ticket submission should load/respond consistently quickly, not intermittently slower than expected.
Actual Result: Confirmed live (and independently by manual testing) that both can be intermittently slow -- sometimes fast, sometimes taking several seconds longer than expected -- rather than a consistent, predictable response time.

Summary: A vehicle can only have one open support ticket at a time across all categories
Description: Attempting to raise a second support ticket for a vehicle that already has any open ticket is rejected with 'Complaint already exists for <vehicle IMEI>' -- confirmed this is NOT scoped to the same category as the existing open ticket: raising a ticket for the same vehicle under a genuinely different category (e.g. an existing 'Device is not giving data' ticket blocks a new 'Odometer is wrong' ticket for the same vehicle) is rejected identically to retrying the same category. Confirmed across 3 independent vehicles, each showing: first ticket succeeds, any subsequent ticket for that vehicle (same or different category) is rejected until the first is closed. This may be an intentional one-active-complaint-per-vehicle business rule rather than a bug, but flagged since it can block legitimately reporting a second, unrelated issue on the same vehicle.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and open Support (Account menu > Support), Raise Ticket for a vehicle with no existing open tickets, pick a category (e.g. 'Device is not giving data'), fill the rest, and submit -- confirm it succeeds.
2. Raise a second ticket for the SAME vehicle, this time picking a DIFFERENT category (e.g. 'Odometer is wrong').
3. Submit and observe the result.
Expected Result: Either both tickets should be allowed (if they represent genuinely different issues), or the rejection message should make clear the restriction is per-vehicle regardless of category, not specific to a duplicate report of the same issue.
Actual Result: The second ticket is rejected with 'Complaint already exists for <vehicle IMEI>', identical to what a genuine same-category duplicate would show, with no indication the block applies across categories too. Confirmed live 3x across 3 different vehicles.

Summary: Complaint already exists error cites the vehicle's raw IMEI instead of the name shown in the selector
Description: When a second ticket for a vehicle is rejected ('Complaint already exists for <IMEI>'), the identifier cited is the vehicle's raw IMEI number (e.g. '864688053444367'), not the plate-style name the Select Vehicles combobox uses to display and select it (e.g. 'ptc400-demo'). A user has no visible way to connect the two, making it look like the block references an unrelated or wrong vehicle. Directly caused real user confusion during testing. RCA across 9 vehicles spanning the full fleet confirmed this is a pure display inconsistency, not a real vehicle-selection/mapping bug: the combobox's displayed value matched the actual selection in 9/9 attempts, each of 5 rejected vehicles cited the exact same IMEI on a repeat attempt (5/5 consistent), and no two different vehicles ever shared a cited IMEI (zero collisions).
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and open Support (Account menu > Support), Raise Ticket for a vehicle that already has an open ticket (or create one first, then try a second).
2. Observe the rejection toast's identifier for the vehicle.
3. Compare it against the vehicle name shown in the Select Vehicles combobox for the same selection.
Expected Result: The rejection message should identify the vehicle the same way the selector does (by name/plate), or include both, so the user can recognize it as the vehicle they just picked.
Actual Result: The rejection cites a raw IMEI number with no visible relationship to the plate-style name shown in the selector, confirmed consistent per-vehicle (not random/wrong) across a 9-vehicle RCA, but still visibly disconnected from what the user selected.

Summary: Admin Panel Create Dealer: "Saler Person" and "Sales Person Contact" are silently mandatory with no asterisk or label association
Description: The Billing Information step's 'Saler Person' (a real typo in the app's own placeholder) and 'Sales Person Contact' fields have no asterisk and no `for` attribute connecting them to their visible label -- same gap already known for several other fields on this wizard (Company Name/GST/PAN/Address/City/PIN Code) -- yet Create Dealer's Submit will not succeed without both being filled with valid-format values. Nothing marks them as required.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open User > Manage Dealer > Create Dealer.
2. Fill Personal Information and click Next.
3. Fill every field that shows a required asterisk on the Billing Information step, deliberately skipping Saler Person and Sales Person Contact (neither is marked required).
4. Attempt to submit.
Expected Result: Fields that are effectively required should be marked with an asterisk like every other required field on the form.
Actual Result: Saler Person and Sales Person Contact show no asterisk and are not reachable via standard label association, despite being effectively mandatory for a successful submission.

Summary: Admin Panel Create/Edit Dealer: PIN Code field has no minimum or maximum length validation
Description: The PIN Code field correctly filters out non-digit characters as typed, but enforces no length bounds: typing 13 digits registers all 13 with no truncation, and typing as few as 2 digits is equally accepted with no minimum-length warning. A real PIN Code is a fixed 6 digits. This is what makes the related Edit-time SQL error (see companion row) reachable in the first place.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open User > Manage Dealer > Create Dealer (or Edit an existing dealer).
2. Type more than 6 digits into a PIN Code field, then separately try fewer than 6.
3. Observe whether either is rejected or truncated.
Expected Result: PIN Code should be capped at exactly 6 digits, matching its real-world format.
Actual Result: Both over-length (13 digits) and under-length (2 digits) values are accepted with no client-side restriction.

Summary: Admin Panel Edit Dealer: an out-of-range PIN Code accepted on Create fails Edit with a raw SQL error (reported by user, not yet independently verified)
Description: A dealer created with a PIN Code longer than 6 digits (nothing prevents this at Create time -- see companion row) later fails when that dealer is edited: submitting the Edit form shows an Edit failed toast, and the Network tab shows a SQL-related error response. A PIN Code shorter than 6 digits does not trigger this failure on Edit, only longer values do. Reported by the user's own manual testing; not yet independently reproduced by automation due to an unrelated test-script timing issue -- needs a follow-up live reverification pass before treating as fully confirmed.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a dealer with a PIN Code longer than 6 digits (e.g. 10 digits).
2. Open that dealer for Edit.
3. Resubmit the Edit form without changing the PIN Code, and check the Network tab for the response.
Expected Result: Edit should either accept the same value Create accepted, or Create should have rejected the out-of-range value in the first place -- either way, a raw SQL error should never reach the client.
Actual Result: Edit fails with an Edit failed toast and a SQL-related error visible in the Network tab, per the user's manual testing.

Summary: Admin Panel Profile: the shared Send OTP mechanism fails with a raw technical error -- blocks both Update Mobile Number and Change Password
Description: Opening My Profile's Mobile field edit (pencil) icon and clicking Send OTP to Current Mobile shows the literal, unmodified HTTP client error 'Http failure response for https://beta2.trackofy.com/user_new.php: 0 Unknown Error'. Confirmed the account's own Change Password flow hits this exact same failure (identical toast, identical endpoint, identical status) when its own Send OTP is clicked -- both features share one broken underlying OTP-send mechanism, not two independent bugs. Status 0 means the request never received a proper HTTP response at all (confirmed via full response capture: no user_new.php call appears among the responses received, only unrelated dashboard calls).
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open My Profile (via the profile icon dropdown).
2. Click the edit (pencil) icon next to Mobile, then Send OTP to Current Mobile -- observe the toast.
3. Separately, open Change Password and click its own Send OTP -- observe the toast.
Expected Result: A safe, generic error message should be shown if the OTP send fails, with no raw HTTP client text or backend endpoint path, for both flows.
Actual Result: Both flows show the literal raw HTTP client error including the backend endpoint path (user_new.php), and no OTP is ever sent for either.
Labels: admin-panel profile information-disclosure raw-error broken-feature change-password

Summary: Admin Panel Create Dealer: submitting an invalid PIN Code silently does nothing -- Submit reports enabled but fires no request and shows no error
Description: With every other field validly filled, injecting a non-numeric value directly into either PIN Code field (bypassing the field's own real-keystroke character filter, which correctly blocks non-numeric input during normal typing) and clicking the still-enabled Create Dealer button produces zero observable effect: no create-dealer API request fires, no toast or inline error appears, the dialog just stays open exactly as before. A fully valid submission in the same session correctly fires the request and succeeds. Note: this specific scenario is not reachable through normal typing (the field's keystroke filter blocks it) -- it would require a non-browser API client or a similar direct-value-injection method, not a real user typing into the form.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open User > Manage Dealer > Create Dealer.
2. Fill every field validly, then set a PIN Code field to a non-numeric value via direct DOM/value injection (not achievable by typing normally).
3. Click Create Dealer (confirmed enabled) and observe network activity and any on-screen feedback.
Expected Result: Either the button should be disabled for an invalid PIN Code, or a clear validation error should appear when Submit is clicked with one.
Actual Result: Clicking Submit with an invalid PIN Code produces zero network activity and zero visible feedback -- confirmed live 2x, against a control confirming a valid submission works normally in the same session.

Summary: CAN Report page has no PDF export button, unlike its sibling Alerts/Unit/Settings pages
Description: After generating a CAN report with real results, the export row shows only Export report to Excel, Export report to CSV, and Copy report content -- no PDF export at all. Confirmed live that CAN Alerts and CAN Unit both have a working Export to PDF button in the identical shared export-row component.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to a CAN-entitled account and open CAN > Reports.
2. Select a protocol and units, generate a report with real results.
3. Inspect the export row for a PDF export option, and compare against CAN > Alerts or CAN > Unit's own export row.
Expected Result: CAN Report should offer the same Excel/CSV/PDF export options as its sibling CAN pages.
Actual Result: Only Excel, CSV, and Copy are present -- no PDF export exists on this page, unlike Alerts and Unit.

Summary: Admin Panel Profile: the Copy icon (Address to Billing Address) in Update Profile does nothing
Description: The Update Profile dialog has a copy icon between the Address and Billing Address sections. Clicking it produces zero observable effect -- every field's value (Address, PIN Code, City, State, Country) is byte-identical before and after the click; the Billing Address section is never overwritten with the Address section's values.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open My Profile, then the main edit (pencil) icon to open Update Profile.
2. Note the Address section's values.
3. Click the copy icon between Address and Billing Address, then compare the Billing Address section's values.
Expected Result: Clicking the copy icon should copy the Address section's values into the Billing Address section.
Actual Result: Every field is byte-identical before and after the click -- the copy icon has no effect at all.

Summary: Admin Panel Profile: Update Profile Picture crashes with a raw PHP/GD error for a technically-imperfect but browser-decodable PNG
Description: Uploading a minimal PNG that every browser tested decodes and displays fine, and that the app's own client-side file picker accepts with no complaint, crashes the server on Update Profile Image: HTTP 500 from /api/update-profile with the raw body {"status":false,"message":"Something went wrong","data":{"error":"imagecreatefrompng(): gd-png: fatal libpng error: IDAT: incorrect data check","line":3461}}. The UI shows only a generic 'Internal Server Error' toast, but the raw PHP function name, library error, and source line are all present in the actual API response. A genuinely valid PNG uploaded immediately afterward via the identical flow succeeded cleanly, confirming this is a real gap in the server's image-processing error handling, not a bad test file.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open My Profile.
2. Click the camera icon (Update Profile Picture) and choose a PNG file that is valid enough for a browser to display but has a subtly malformed data stream.
3. Click Update Profile Image and inspect the Network tab response.
Expected Result: The server should validate/re-encode the image safely and either accept it or return a clean, generic validation error -- never a raw PHP/library error with internal details.
Actual Result: The server returns a raw PHP/GD error (function name, library message, source line) in the API response body, surfaced to the user only as a generic 'Internal Server Error' toast.

Summary: Admin Panel Profile: Address/City/State/Country/PIN Code fields have zero input validation -- live account data already contains garbage values
Description: Typing pure digits into the City field via real keystrokes registers completely with no character filtering or format validation. The account's own real, currently-saved profile data already contains exactly this class of garbage: Country='223232313213123' (a number), Billing PIN Code='67238052e23232' (mixed alphanumeric), Billing City='6723805sdsd' (garbage), Billing State='6723805' (a number), Billing Country='6723805' (a number) -- proving this isn't just a client-side gap, since this data is already persisted in the real account record.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open My Profile, then the main edit (pencil) icon to open Update Profile.
2. Type pure digits into the City field and observe whether they're accepted.
3. Separately, inspect the real (pre-existing) values already in the Country/Billing PIN Code/Billing City/Billing State/Billing Country fields.
Expected Result: Address-shaped fields (City, State, Country) should reject or filter numeric input; PIN Code should be numeric-only with a fixed length. None of this should be reachable via normal use, and no garbage should already exist in saved data.
Actual Result: Digits are accepted into City with no validation, and the real saved profile already contains numeric/garbage values in Country, Billing PIN Code, Billing City, Billing State, and Billing Country -- confirming no validation exists anywhere in the pipeline.

Summary: Admin Panel: Brand/Model images served over plain HTTP from an HTTPS page fail to load everywhere
Description: Every brand image URL is http://beta2.trackofy.com/... (plain HTTP) while the app itself runs entirely on https://staging.trackofy.com and its own API calls go to https://beta2.trackofy.com -- the classic mixed-content pattern, which browsers silently block/fail to load. Checked all 6 images on the Brand list (5 pre-existing plus 1 created live): all 6 report naturalWidth/naturalHeight of 0 (a definitively broken load), despite the browser reporting the load complete. Independently confirmed by the user's own manual testing that the Edit Brand wizard's image preview also fails to load the existing logo.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open Configuration > Manage Brand.
2. Observe any brand row's logo image in the table.
3. Open Edit on any brand and observe its image preview.
Expected Result: Brand/Model logo images should load and display correctly in both the list table and the Edit wizard.
Actual Result: Every brand image (6/6 checked) fails to load -- naturalWidth/naturalHeight of 0 -- because its URL is served over plain HTTP instead of HTTPS, and the same failure was independently confirmed in the Edit wizard.

Summary: Admin Panel Documentation Create Category: Create button has no required-field gating at all
Description: Opening Documentation's Create Category dialog fresh (Category Name*, Slug*, Sort Order*, Status* all marked required) shows the Create button already enabled with every field completely empty -- unlike the equivalent Create Brand, Create Model, and Create Menu dialogs in the same Configuration tab, which all correctly keep Submit disabled until required fields are filled.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open Configuration > Documentation.
2. Click Add/Create to open the Create Category dialog.
3. Without filling any field, check whether the Create button is enabled.
Expected Result: Create should stay disabled until every field marked with a required asterisk is filled, matching the sibling Brand/Model/Menu forms.
Actual Result: Create reports as enabled immediately on dialog open, before any field is touched.

Summary: Admin Panel: /admin/billing/dashboard silently redirects to /admin/dashboard
Description: Navigating directly to /admin/billing/dashboard -- a real, linked destination from the panel's own nav/menus -- silently lands on the generic /admin/dashboard instead, with no error or explanation. Same symptom already reported and now fixed for Configuration's Manage Brand/Manage Model/Documentation and the top-level Menu page; this route was not part of that original list and still shows the same broken pattern.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel.
2. Navigate directly to /admin/billing/dashboard (or via any in-app link pointing to it).
3. Observe the final URL and rendered page.
Expected Result: Should load a real Billing Dashboard page.
Actual Result: Silently redirects to /admin/dashboard instead, confirmed live 3x via an automated test loop.

Summary: Admin Panel: inconsistent sign-out control labels between desktop and mobile
Description: Two separate, redundant sign-out controls exist with different labels. The desktop-visible one is the profile icon (top-right) dropdown, which shows a red 'Sign Out' option -- confirmed working (session is genuinely invalidated server-side afterward). A second, separate nav item literally labeled 'Logout' also exists but is CSS-gated mobile-only, invisible at any standard desktop width and only reachable via a hamburger toggle that itself only appears at narrow (<=768px) viewports.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel at a standard desktop width and click the profile icon (top-right) -- note the 'Sign Out' label.
2. Resize the browser to a mobile width (e.g. 390px) and open the hamburger nav menu -- note the 'Logout' label on the equivalent control.
Expected Result: The sign-out control should use one consistent label regardless of viewport.
Actual Result: Two redundant controls exist with two different labels ('Sign Out' on desktop, 'Logout' on mobile), confirmed live via DOM inspection at both widths and independently via screenshot.

Summary: Admin Panel Profile: old photo reportedly still shown in "profile menu" after updating profile picture (reported by user, not yet independently reproduced)
Description: User reported that after successfully updating the profile picture, the old photo is still visible in what they described as the "profile menu" instead of the new one. Three separate automated reproduction attempts did not reproduce this: (1) upload new photo then navigate away and back via the profile-icon menu with no hard reload -- the avatar src picked up the new cache-busting timestamp correctly; (2) upload new photo then do a full hard page reload -- same correct result; (3) the profile dropdown menu opened from the header person icon (containing "My Profile"/"Sign Out") was checked directly and contains zero elements on any page, so it cannot itself be showing a stale photo. Needs the user to clarify exactly which element shows the old photo, and whether it needs a full refresh or a different tab/device to reproduce, before this can be independently confirmed.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in to the Admin Panel and open My Profile.
2. Update the profile picture to a new image and confirm the success toast.
3. Open the "profile menu" (exact element not yet pinned down) and observe whether it shows the old or new photo.
Expected Result: The profile menu/avatar should always reflect the most recently uploaded photo.
Actual Result: Per the user, the old photo is still shown; not yet reproduced independently across 3 automated attempts (SPA nav, hard reload, and direct inspection of the profile dropdown, which has no image at all).
